head: 10 new productivity apps climbing the App Store this week
dek: These productivity apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Productivity charts this week, from a 3D CAD app to focus timers, planners and a family chore chart.
where: iPhone and iPad, US App Store Productivity charts (paid, plus Namecheap Private Email in free) this week
means: If your to-do app isn't working for you, these are new planners, timers and work tools people in the US are trying right now.
todo: Look at each App Store page before you buy: Hello Dayish mentions a subscription after a free trial, and FocusBook and DeskOS are built around the iPhone Duo.

list.name: PaliCAD
list.what: A 3D CAD app for iPad and iPhone with 2D sketching, solid modeling and common CAD file formats.

list.name: FocusBook
list.what: A focus timer that starts when you open your iPhone Duo or turn any iPhone sideways.

list.name: Hello Dayish
list.what: A daily planner that starts by asking what kind of day you're having: green, yellow or red.

list.name: ScreenRecess: Gentle Rhythm
list.what: Gives a group of apps one shared time allowance, then pauses them for a timed break.

list.name: Tallied Time Tracker
list.what: A time tracker where you press Start and Stop on a task, with weekly totals and CSV export.

list.name: ChartMe: Family Chore Chart
list.what: A family chore chart where kids check off chores on their own device and earn points for rewards.

list.name: MyLilMatrix
list.what: Sorts tasks into four boxes by importance and urgency, with subtasks, reminders and widgets.

list.name: DeskOS
list.what: A desktop-style workspace with files, a browser and creative tools; on iPhone Duo it shows a keyboard and trackpad below the fold.

list.name: CalenCards
list.what: Plans the day as a deck of cards you swipe away when they're done.

list.name: Namecheap Private Email
list.what: Namecheap's email app for addresses on your own domain, with AI-drafted replies.
